Decision made by the user 2026-09-15 and written into SPECS.md #13 in form (b): afox needs a gate of its own. Ticket closure in Jira or Beads was rejected as the gate. The user specified the cycle in full - DEVELOPER claims done, TESTER tests, REVIEWER reviews only once green, DEVELOPER triages each finding as implement, file or reject, TESTER retests, a failed retest that causes a code change starts a new review cycle, and a fourth cycle is elevated to ARCHITECT to settle. The Beads ticket closes only when settled. Local only, no CI in scope. The user also fixed the pane lifecycle in the same answer: ORCHESTRATOR respawns DEVELOPER, TESTER and REVIEWER per ticket, ORCHESTRATOR is never closed, ARCHITECT persists. Two follow-up build tickets exist and are named in SPECS.md #13: afox-99q for the cycle, afox-2fc for the pane lifecycle. No code was written for this ticket.

Confirmed working on a booted fleet, session afox, 2026-09-15. Root cause of the old result: peers were reachable all along, but ListAgents showed them under auto-generated session names, so SendMessage to a role name could not resolve. First attempt this session reproduced it exactly - ListAgents returned 11 peer sessions including the fleet panes, and SendMessage to DEVELOPER failed with 'No agent named DEVELOPER is reachable'. fleet.sh now passes claude --name <ROLE>, which was verified to exist before it was wired. After that change: ORCHESTRATOR called ListAgents and got DEVELOPER and ARCHITECT listed by role name with their tmux pane ids, then called SendMessage to DEVELOPER with the planted codename MARMOT-7. DEVELOPER's pane showed 'Message from @ORCHESTRATOR: CODENAME MARMOT-7' and the codename appears three times in DEVELOPER's own session log. Both send and receipt captured, from the two sessions' own logs rather than the screen. Agent-initiated: tmux send-keys carried only the human instruction into ORCHESTRATOR, never the agent-to-agent hop. Limit recorded in README and SPECS.md #10: the channel is a Claude Code feature and reaches claude panes only; codex and devin panes do not appear in ListAgents. README Unverified entry deleted and replaced with a Peer messaging section, SPECS.md #10 moved to Met.

Board pane observed live in the fleet window, session afox, 2026-09-15, and confirmed by the user. board.mjs runs as its own pane beside ORCHESTRATOR, refreshes from 'bd list --all --flat --json' on a timer, and draws one line per ticket: empty box for open, tilde for in progress, ticked box plus the strikethrough code for closed, with a done-count header. It runs no agent, so it costs nothing and is deliberately left out of the cost manifest. fleet.sh adds it unless FLEET_BOARD=off, and a window with no room for one more pane prints a note instead of failing.

Written finding is in ACTIVE-LISTENING.md in the working tree, and SPECS.md #11 is updated. Answer: yes, buildable - and for claude panes it already works with no new code, on top of the channel confirmed in afox-3u9.3. Observed 2026-09-15 from both panes' own session logs: 07:39:31 DEVELOPER started a ~60s shell task and its turn ended while the task ran; ORCHESTRATOR then sent it 'URGENT PIVOT - stop what you are doing and reply PIVOT immediately'; 07:39:56 DEVELOPER took the message mid-task, replied PIVOT, and explicitly declined to abandon the work - 'Did not stop your tick command, peer cannot cancel your task'; 07:40:32 it returned to the task and reported all 30 lines of output. Interrupt, own decision, resume, no human in the delivery path. Two limits recorded rather than glossed: a peer message is picked up on a turn boundary, not mid-generation, which for afox's roles is the same thing in practice because Claude Code backgrounds long shell work and ends the turn; and the channel reaches claude panes only, so a mixed-provider fleet has this for some roles and not others. Recommendation in the finding: build nothing, spend the effort on the merge gate afox-99q.
